# Privacy deny-list — patterns that must never appear in this repository.
#
# This repository is public: it ships a product, never its author's data.
# CI fails on a match (see .github/workflows/privacy.yml); the same scan runs
# from scripts/privacy-scan.sh, and a pre-commit hook can call it too.
#
# This file is itself public, so it contains PATTERNS, not secrets — identifier
# *shapes* rather than real identifiers. The author's own vocabulary (names,
# hostnames, serials, the exports that were used to build the parsers) belongs
# in .github/privacy-denylist.local.txt, which is gitignored and reaches CI
# from the PRIVACY_DENYLIST_LOCAL repository secret so the job still runs it.
#
# Format: one extended-regex per line. Blank lines and lines starting with #
# are ignored. Paths listed in .privacyignore are excluded from the scan.

# --- The project's former name -----------------------------------------------
# The public repository exists under a new name, and this is the check that
# keeps it that way — it catches a stray env var, a database file, an InfluxDB
# tag or a UI string reintroduced from an older tree. Both spellings are here:
# the full name, and the short three-letter front-end prefix it used for its
# CSS custom properties, its `data-` attributes and its JS global. Word
# boundaries keep the second from matching the middle of an unrelated token.
#
# Both patterns spell their distinguishing letter as a character class. That is
# not obfuscation for its own sake: this file is scanned by the very pattern it
# holds, so a literal here would make the repository fail its own check, and
# `grep -ri <former name> .` — the acceptance test for this whole exercise —
# has to come back empty.
dat(a)?lheim
\bd[l]h\b
\bD[L]H\b

# --- Personal identifiers ----------------------------------------------------
# Generic shapes only. Specific names and addresses belong in the local
# supplement described above.
[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@(gmail|outlook|hotmail|yahoo|proton)\.[a-z]{2,}
\+[0-9]{2}\s?[0-9]{9,}

# --- Infrastructure details --------------------------------------------------
# One writer per deployment: internal hostnames, private addresses and
# secret-store paths belong to the deployment repository, never here.
# Variable NAMES are fine; values are not.
\b(10|192\.168)\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\.[0-9]{1,3}\b
# Internal hostnames only in host position — a bare "\.local\b" also matches
# filename globs like *.local.* and denylist.local.txt, which are not hostnames.
(https?://|@|[[:space:]])[a-z0-9-]+\.(local|lan|internal)([:/[:space:]]|$)
(vault|secret)/(data|kv)/
kubeconfig
